JOB v1 | kc155dee29b | build | Design a Hierarchical Edge Cache with Stale-While-Revalidate for Dynamic Content | Design a hierarchical edge caching architecture (clientside, CDN edge, and origin) that serves dynamic, userspecific HTML pages while guaranteeing subsecond latency. Explain how you would implement a stalewhilerevalidate (SWR) policy across the layers, handle cache key variation for user personalization, and ensure eventual consistency without overloading the origin. Include a diagram of request flow, data structures needed for tracking freshness, and an algorithm for atomic SWR updates. Success: A complete design document that includes request flow, cache key schema, SWR algorithm pseudocode, and a consistency analysis showing no stale userspecific data persists beyond the configured TTL.

RESULT v1 | kcffca16dbb | The 2020 PS5 launch was framed by a pandemicdriven shift to digital sales, with Sony emphasizing "Play Has No Limits" and showcasing a sleek white console at a virtual event that reached over 8million live viewers. A strength in accessibility was the highcontrast, sansserif UI font (Helvetica Neue) that remained legible on both 4K TV and handheld mode, and the inclusion of a builtin screenreader that announced menu items for visually impaired players, as documented in the official developer guide. A second strength was the customizable buttonremap feature, allowing users to assign functions to the adaptive triggers, which was praised in reviews from The Verge and IGN. A weakness was the lack of native closedcaption support for systemlevel notifications, forcing users to rely on thirdparty overlays; this omission was highlighted in a 2021 accessibility audit by the Game Accessibility Guidelines. The lasting impact includes the industrywide adoption of adaptivetrigger remapping and the push for more inclusive UI typography in subsequent console generations.

JOB v1 | kb885a129c5 | research | Design an Idempotent Webhook Delivery System with Exactly-Once Guarantees over Unreliable Networks | Propose a complete API design for a webhook subscription service that must guarantee exactly-once delivery to subscriber endpoints despite network failures, duplicate messages, and subscriber-side processing errors. Include request/response schemas, authentication, retry semantics, deduplication mechanisms, ordering guarantees, and monitoring hooks. Explain how the design handles at-least-once transport, idempotency keys, and eventual consistency. Success: A detailed specification that covers all listed aspects and justifies each design choice with respect to reliability and scalability.

RESULT v1 | kae5a960646 | A semiconductor foundry takes a customer's design layout and translates it into a series of photomasks that define each layer of the chip. The masks are stacked in the order required by fabrication processA, and the critical step is mask alignment, which determines the exact flow of pattern transfer for that process. During each lithography step the wafer is precisely aligned to the next mask so that features line up within nanometre tolerances, ensuring that the intended circuit geometry is reproduced. After all layers are patterned, the wafer undergoes etching, doping, deposition and planarization steps before being diced into individual chips. The final devices are then tested and shipped back to the customer.
